full_judgment: 6. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record interfered with the judgments of the Courts below on the reasoning’s that since the plaintiffs failed to prove part payment of consideration amount, they are not entitled to a decree for specific performance even if it is proved the defendant has executed the deed of contract. The learned Judges of the High Court Division having found fault in the judgments of the Courts below reassessed the relevant evidence of Sree Khokan Chandra. Mondal (PW.1), Nawab Ali (P.W.2), Shaheb Ali (P.W.3) and SK. Maminul Islam (P.W.4) and observed that the Courts below erred in law in believing the execution of the contract for talc in failing to consider that the plaintiffs did not examine the scribe and that they illegally believed P.W.3 the only witness examined to corroborate the plaintiffs claim, who had got admitted enmity with the defendant and that P.W.4 had admitted that he had no idea about transaction made between the plaintiffs and the defendant, and had arrived at the conclusion that "the impugned judgment and order suffer from misconception and mis-appreciation of law, inasmuch as, the plaint does not contain the facts regarding offer, acceptance, time and place of the baina and also the names of witnesses as required…….. Further in a suit for specific performance of contract the payment of consideration of money is also a material fact and as already been discussed, no reliable witness supported the payment of consideration money. But the trial court did not at all discuss this question of payment of consideration and the appellate Court, without discussing the evidence at all made a sweeping remark about consideration".
